notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l009: The proper name Туган is a close reading of the joined medial letters and is absent from the nearby abridged printed witness. Completion-first direct manuscript transcription; uncertain forms and provisional English are queued for later review.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l010: жалгыздан is visually likely, but the final morphology and implied lineage sense remain provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l014: Алган is the likeliest opening word, but the phrase is compressed and the English is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l023: көөдөн is a contextual reading of a heavily joined word; the visible letter forms do not make every vowel secure.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l024: Ардактаган is the most plausible reading of the lightly written opening word.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l025: жете is visually plausible, but the idiom and its relationship to кайтар are uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf014:l027: балдыз is a difficult cursive reading and the object of алар is implicit; the English remains provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l006: The opening phrase is a best-effort reading of lightly written, joined cursive; дүрбөтүп is contextually plausible but not fully secure.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l007: Карбайгандар is the closest visible reading, but the lexeme and therefore the English are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l008: The three-noun reading fits the visible letter groups, though the middle word and inflection are faint.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l011: The manuscript appears to compress the phrase as төрт түлүгү белен экен; the last two words are lightly formed and the English is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l020: Токтоп is the likeliest reading of the first word; its internal letters are faint.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l021: The first two words are fairly clear, but the closing phrase resembles мураа үй and remains unresolved; the English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l027: This manuscript-only line is faint. Азууларын эр кайтарган is a letter-shape reading; both syntax and English remain provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l028: The line appears to read Астынкы эрдин шаңдаткан, but the final verb is heavily joined and may be another related form.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf015:l029: The baseline is fully visible but pale. Ордодогу and the idiomatic койкоңдоткон are best-effort readings; the middle word and translation are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l002: The phrase is contextually clear, but the middle letters of Маңдайынан are lightly and tightly written.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l005: The final word looks like нар and suits the camel description; the compressed letters could admit another reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l007: A crossed-out word precedes the retained baseline; аргымак is the best reading of the replacement phrase.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l008: The manuscript appears to read Нардан; the case form and resulting English are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l009: The final verb is faint; өткөрдү is the best contextual reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l010: мөңгү is a tentative letter-shape reading of an unresolved word; the English is only contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l012: The short line is pale; Алдоону издеген is a best-effort reading and its connection to the feast passage is unclear.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l013: күтүрүп is the likeliest reading of the joined medial letters; the idiomatic English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l016: The line visually reads Эки казына ак койдун, but the construction is unusual and the English remains literal.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l018: караң контуруп is an unresolved reading of strongly joined handwriting; the English is a literal provisional rendering.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l019: ара is the visible reading, but the phrase may contain a different word division; translation is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l020: The first word appears to be Кайнаган, though its relation to бээ is semantically uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l021: The line appears to repeat үч around өркөчүн; both transcription and syntax are uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l024: Капкалаган is a tentative reading of a corrected and overwritten word; the English conveys the apparent sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l025: кымын is an unresolved manuscript lexeme and may be a different word; the English is highly provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l026: үйкөө is a best-effort reading of an unclear word; syntax and English are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l027: кымын remains unresolved as on line 25; English follows the apparent distribution context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l029: басыптыр is visually likely, but the idiomatic sense in this passage is uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf016:l030: The opening word is faint but appears to be Баары; this final baseline continues syntactically onto the next page.
